# २३. हे प्रच्छक अ: क्या फिक्र करोगे तुम्हें
खुशखबरी होनेवाली है कई सो गई अब
र.खर ही अब बहुत दे गा वही मनोरथ पूर्ण हों-
गे परन्तु एक फिक्र मार्ग दीखे है ऊपर से
खर्च आवे है पास धन विशेष नहीं दीखता
परन्तु चिंता मत करना काम बडा इज्जत के
साथ बनेगा और कई जगह से लाभ होगा
करनेवाला और है वही फिक्र कर रहा है अब
विशेष लाभ की सूरत होगी मित्र में चित्त
बहुत रहना है वे भी चित्त से प्यार कर रहे हैं अब
तुम शीघ्र इस कार्य की सिद्धि चाहो तो श्री
गंगाजी के ५ ब्राह्मणों को खांड के जिमाओ
और सठ्ठी चावल दही दान करो काम शीघ्र
फत्ते होगा और गुप्त लाभ होगा घर में चांद-
ना होगा एक काम गुप्त से गुप्त न किस
बनाया सो ईश्वर का ध्यान रखे करो।
translation:
<meta>This page continues the series of divinations or "immediate questions" (tatkalik prashna) posed to the practitioner, Hardev. The tone remains advisory and prophetic.</meta>

# 23. O Inquirer: Why do you worry? You
are about to receive good news. Much has already passed;
now, much will be given. Your heart's desires will be
fulfilled. However, one worry appears on your path:
expenses are coming from above, and there does not appear to be much wealth at hand.
But do not worry; the work will be accomplished with
great honor <note>izzat: social standing or prestige</note>, and profit will come from many places.
The One who acts is someone else <note>A reference to Divine providence or a higher power</note>; He is already taking care of the worry. Now,
there will be a prospect of special profit. Your mind
dwells much on your friends; they too love you from their hearts. Now,
if you desire the swift success <term>siddhi</term> <note>the successful completion of a task or spiritual attainment</note> of this work, then
feed sugar to five Brahmins <note>priestly class</note> of the Holy Ganges,
and donate "Satthi" rice <note>a variety of rice that matures in sixty days, often used in rituals</note> and curd. The work will be
victorious <note>phatte: victory or success</note> quickly and there will be hidden profit. There will be
light in the house. One task was kept most secret from everyone;
keep your focus on God.

<summary>This page offers a reassuring prophecy to an inquirer facing financial stress, promising honorable success and suggesting specific charitable acts to ensure a favorable outcome.</summary>
<keywords>divination, Hardev, prophecy, charity, Brahmins, success, financial worry, ritual offerings</keywords>

<meta>The text continues the alchemical poem from the previous page, shifting from the metaphor of a garden to the metaphor of "The Sword" and the "Afterlife Creation." It maintains the theme of transformation through nature-based allegories.</meta>

->A SYMBOL<-

### THE SWORD

<note>original: "al-sayf"</note>
You see it like rose-colored amber in its hue,
and it turns white like camphor if transparency touches it.
<note>In alchemy, amber often represents the "Red Work" (rubedo) and camphor represents the "White Work" (albedo).</note>

And when the sun kindles the fire of its rays upon it,
it continues to elevate what it discharges and reveals.
<note>This describes the process of sublimation or distillation using solar heat.</note>

<margin>The level ground of the earth</margin>
<gloss>meaning the rain</gloss> <gloss>poured</gloss> <gloss>meaning from the clouds</gloss> <gloss>the plural of "hadba," which is the mountain</gloss>
The flooding rain pierced the plateaus through the dripping,
turning them into level, empty plains.

<margin>With the deterrent within it, it does not need that</margin>

### THE SWORD

<margin>in it</margin>
<gloss>Gemini is a fruit</gloss>
<note>The term "Gemini" (al-Jawza') here likely refers to an alchemical ingredient or a specific astrological timing for the experiment.</note>
And Gemini rained stars into it,
and the shaking revealed what the sinking had hidden.

There, an afterlife creation returned
for its bodies, in which they find familiarity with their spirits.
<note>Alchemists often described the "reanimation" of dead matter as a spiritual resurrection.</note>

<margin>Address</margin>
They revolve as if time loves their newness,
so it has no transgression against them nor any diversion.

That is a resurrection without gathering or spreading,
as if the eternal exiles were a slow march within it.
<note>original: "nufaah." This refers to discarded or purged materials that are "reborn" in the alchemical process.</note>

If you are one who seeks to decipher our symbol,
do so with diligence, and do not let the description lead your intellect astray.

Do not let the eggs distract you from all our peels,
our oils, the hair, the blood, and the skull.

<gloss>The hoof</gloss>
Nor the bone, the biles, the urine, and the filth,
nor the feathers, the furs, the dung, and the hoof.
<note>This list refers to the "Animal Stone" path of alchemy, where practitioners sought the elixir within organic waste and biological materials.</note>

<meta>The catchword at the bottom of the page is "nor striking."</meta>

<summary>This page uses the metaphor of "The Sword" and "Resurrection" to describe the refinement of matter. The author warns the reader to look past literal descriptions of organic materials like hair and blood to find the true alchemical secret.</summary>

<keywords>The Sword, Amber, Camphor, Gemini, Afterlife Creation, Resurrection, Animal Stone, Organic Alchemy</keywords>

الملك وقال لحكماء بابل اي رجل يقرأُ هذه الكتابة ويبين لي تفسيرها فانهُ
يلبسُ الارجوان وقلادة من ذهب في عنقهِ ويتسلط ثالثاً في المملكة
٨ * ثم دخل كل حكماءِ الملك فلم يستطيعوا ان يقرأوا الكتابة ولا ان
٩ يعرفوا الملك بتفسيرها * ففزع الملك بيلشاصر جداً وتغيرت فيهِ هيئتُهُ
١٠ واضطرب عظماؤُهُ * اما الملكة فلسبب كلام الملك وعظمائهِ دخلت
بيت الوليمة فاجابت الملكة وقالت ايها الملك عِش الى الابد .
١١ لا تفزعك افكارك ولا تتغير هيئتُك * يوجد في مملكتك رجل فيهِ روح
الآلهة القدوسين وفي ايام ابيك وُجِدَت فيهِ نيرة وفطنة وحكمة كحكمة الآلهة
والملك نبوخذنصر ابوك جعلهُ كبير المجوس والسحرة والكلدانيين والمنجمين .
١٢ ابوك الملك * من حيث ان روحاً فاضلة ومعرفة وفطنة وتعبير الاحلام وتبيين
الغاز وحل عقد وُجِدَت في دانيال هذا الذي سماهُ الملك بلطشاصر .

->فليدع الآن دانيال فيبين التفسير<-

١٣ حينئذٍ أُدخل دانيال الى قدام الملك . فاجاب الملك وقال لدانيال
أنت هو دانيال من بني سبي يهوذا الذي جلبهُ ابي الملك من يهوذا
١٤ * قد سمعت عنك ان فيك روح الآلهة وان فيك نيرة وفطنة وحكمة
١٥ فاضلة * والآن أُدخل قدامي الحكماء والسحرة ليقرأوا هذه الكتابة ويعرفوني
١٦ بتفسيرها فلم يستطيعوا ان يبينوا تفسير الكلام * وانا قد سمعت عنك
انك تستطيع ان تفسر تفسيراً وتحل عقداً . فان استطعت الآن ان تقرأ
الكتابة وتعرفني بتفسيرها فتلبس الارجوان وقلادة من ذهب في عنقك
وتتسلط ثالثاً في المملكة
١٧ فاجاب دانيال وقال قدام الملك . لتكن عطاياك لنفسك وهَبْ
١٨ هباتك لغيري . لكني اقرأ الكتابة للملك واعرفهُ بالتفسير * انت ايها
الملك فالله العلي اعطى اباك نبوخذنصر ملكوتاً وعظمةً وجلالاً وبهاءً
١٩ * وللعظمة التي اعطاهُ اياها كانت ترتعد وتفزع قدامهُ جميع الشعوب والامم

<meta>This page continues Chapter 5 of the Book of Daniel, following the appearance of the mysterious handwriting on the wall during Belshazzar’s feast. The previous page ended with the King calling for his wise men after being terrified by the supernatural event.</meta>

# Daniel * 5 *
<page-num>1196</page-num>

the King and said to the wise men of Babylon, "Any man who reads this writing and shows me its interpretation shall be
clothed in <term>purple</term><note>A color reserved for royalty and high-ranking officials due to the extreme expense of the dye.</note> and have a necklace of gold around his neck, and shall rule as third in the kingdom."
٨ * Then all the King's wise men entered, but they were not able to read the writing, nor to
٩ make known the interpretation to the King. * Then King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, and his appearance was changed,
١٠ and his nobles were troubled. * As for the Queen, because of the words of the King and his nobles, she entered
the banquet hall; and the Queen answered and said, "O King, live forever.
١١ Do not let your thoughts terrify you, nor let your appearance change. * There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the
holy gods. In the days of your father, light and understanding and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him;
and King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, made him chief of the <term>magi</term>, sorcerers, <term>Chaldeans</term><note>In this context, a class of learned scholars and astrologers in Babylon.</note>, and astrologers.
١٢ Your father the King [did this] * because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, the interpreting of dreams, the explaining
of riddles, and the solving of riddles were found in this Daniel, whom the King named Belteshazzar.

->Let Daniel be called now, and he will show the interpretation<-

١٣ Then Daniel was brought in before the King. And the King answered and said to Daniel,
"Are you that Daniel, one of the captives of Judah, whom my father the King brought from Judah?
١٤ * I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light, understanding, and excellent
١٥ wisdom are found in you. * And now the wise men and sorcerers were brought before me to read this writing and make known
١٦ to me its interpretation, but they could not show the interpretation of the words. * And I have heard of you,
that you are able to give interpretations and solve riddles. Now if you are able to read
the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed in purple and have a necklace of gold around your neck,
and shall rule as third in the kingdom."
١٧ Then Daniel answered and said before the King, "Let your gifts be for yourself, and give
١٨ your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the King and make known to him the interpretation. * As for you, O
King, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.
١٩ * And because of the greatness that He gave him, all peoples and nations trembled and feared before him."

<summary>King Belshazzar's wise men fail to interpret the writing on the wall, leading the Queen to recommend Daniel, who is then summoned and offered high honors which he initially refuses.</summary>
<keywords>Daniel, Babylon, Belshazzar, Nebuchadnezzar, Belteshazzar, purple, Magi, sorcerers, Chaldeans, astrologers, Judah</keywords>

<meta>This page serves as a theological and philosophical bridge, linking the Christian doctrine of the Holy Trinity to the composition of the Philosophers' Stone. It establishes the "Universal" principle before transitioning into the specific alchemical authorities, namely Basilius Valentinus, to justify the "death" (transformation) of gold.</meta>

# 138 The Green Lion,

The person in the Holy Trinity is God the Holy Spirit, a comforter from our Lord Jesus Christ, who strengthens and comforts his faithful Christians, so that they believe in him for eternal life. So it is also with the spirit and the Matter of the Mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿, referring here to the "mercurial" or fluidic essence of matter</note> Body: for when they come together, it is then called a doubled Mercury <term>Mercury duplicatus</term> <note>a "doubled" mercury, indicating a substance that has been joined with its own internal spirit or another metallic essence</note>, which are then two spirits: God the Father, and God the Holy Spirit; but God the Son is the Glorified Man <note>original: "Homo glorificatus"</note>, resembling our own glorified and fixed Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> of the Philosophers' Stone <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>. Therefore this Stone is also called Threefold <note>original: "Trinus"</note>, namely originating from two Waters or Spirits, the Mineral and the Vegetable, to which an Animal Fire <note>symbol: △; the "animal" refers to the third kingdom of nature, often associated with the soul or blood</note> Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> is added. These are then two and three, and yet only one. If you do not understand this, you shall achieve nothing. Thus I have sufficiently described the Universal <note>The "Universal" refers to the Great Work or the fundamental medicine that applies to all things</note> to you through comparison: pray to God for his blessing; for without him you shall find nothing. Amen.

That I have included this reasoning from Basilius <note>Basilius Valentinus: a legendary 15th-century alchemical authority whose "Twelve Keys" are foundational to the craft</note> here, was done to prove that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> must die just as well as the other metals. And although there are many who say that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> cannot die, nevertheless Basilius here informs us that Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> dies through the Mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> of the Philosophers; and that this Fire <note>symbol: △</note> and Water <note>symbol: ▽</note> open the Gold and cause it to die. Of this Water <note>symbol: ▽</note> he has spoken in his 2nd and 3rd Key, and teaches

<summary>This page explains the alchemical composition of the Philosophers' Stone through an allegory of the Holy Trinity and cites Basilius Valentinus to argue that gold must undergo a symbolic "death" to be transformed.</summary>
<keywords>Holy Trinity, Mercury, Gold, Philosophers' Stone, Basilius Valentinus, Threefold Stone, Alchemical Death, Universal Medicine</keywords>

But geometry corresponds to the <term>triad</term> <gloss>the number three</gloss>, not only because it is occupied with the three-dimensional and its parts and forms, but also because it is peculiar to this teacher always to name surfaces, which indeed they used to call colors, as geometry reaching its term, since geometry is concerned primarily with the plane surface. And the most elementary plane surface consists in a triad of either angles or sides, from which, as if from a certain base toward a single point when depth is added, the most elementary of solid bodies, the pyramid, is in turn constituted. It is bounded by the minimum of four angles or lines, fitted together by three equal intervals, after which no other body exists naturally in solid space. And spherical science <note>astronomy</note> is fitted to the <term>tetrad</term> <gloss>the number four</gloss>; for of all bodies the sphere is naturally the most complete, the most encompassing of all others, and superior in countless other respects. It is an enclosure of four things: center, diameter, circumference, and solid volume, that is to say, resistance to touch. Because it is of such a nature, the men used to swear by Pythagoras through it, obviously admiring and singing his praises for the discovery, just as Empedocles also says somewhere:

> "No, by him who handed down to our generation the <term>tetractys</term> <gloss>the sacred quaternary</gloss>,

### Jagüey

## CLXXVIII

### Jaltepeque

*Jaltepeques* llaman nuestros salineros á los cerritos de *arena dulce* que se forman en las salinas con los residuos que quedan después de extraer la sal á la arena bañada por el mar. Recuerdo que estando yo en el puerto del Triunfo, y tratando de encontrar un punto desde el cual pudieran verse los volcanes de San Vicente y de San Miguel, me dijo un individuo: "tal vez señor, desde esos *jaltepeques* pudiera Ud. ver esos picos." (1)

El sustantivo *jaltepeque* se deriva de la lengua nahuatl: se compone de *xalli* (*jal-li*)="arena," y de *tepetl*= "cerro;" significa, pues, "cerro de arena."

Estos vocablos *xalli* y *tepetl* son de origen quiché: el primero de ellos se compone de *tza*="cosa salobre," y de *lil*, raíz de *litil*="llano, plano;" de

---

(1) En la hermosa bahía que está al Sur de Zacatecoluca se ha trabajado la sal desde hace muchísimos años, y probablemente á los numerosos montones de arena que fueron formándose en los bordes de la bahía, se daba el nombre de *Jaltepeque*, ó "Bahía de los *jaltepeques*" con que la conocemos.

De *xalli* se deriva *xaxalteyo*="pedregoso, lugar de piedras menudas."

# J

## CLXXVII

### Jagüey

(See the article *Chagüite*.)

## CLXXVIII

### Jaltepeque

Our salt-makers call *jaltepeques* the little mounds of *fresh sand* <note>original: "arena dulce," that is, sand from which the salt has been removed</note> that form in the salt works from the leftovers that remain after the salt is extracted from sand soaked by the sea. I remember that once, when I was at the port of El Triunfo trying to find a spot from which the volcanoes of San Vicente and San Miguel could be seen, a man said to me: "Perhaps, sir, you might see those peaks from those *jaltepeques*." (1)

The noun *jaltepeque* derives from the Nahuatl language. It is made up of *xalli* (*jal-li*), "sand," and *tepetl*, "hill"; it therefore means "hill of sand."

These words *xalli* and *tepetl* are of K'iche' origin. The first is made up of *tza*, "brackish thing," and *lil*, root of *litil*, "plain, flat"; so

---

(1) In the beautiful bay south of Zacatecoluca, salt has been worked for a great many years. Probably the many heaps of sand that gradually formed along the shores of the bay were called *Jaltepeque*, whence the name "Bay of the *jaltepeques*" by which we know it.

From *xalli* derives *xaxalteyo*, "stony, a place of small stones."

den Teppich! das, was dabei vorgeht, deutet die unvermuthete Nachricht an, die sich von der Verfolgung aller Obern des Tempelordens und dem ihm beigebrachten tödtlichen Streiche verbreitete.

Der Candidat, wenn er vor den Meister gestellt ist, wird ungestüm gefragt; man prüft seine Beständigkeit, u. s. w. Dies ist ein abermaliges Sinnbild von der unmenschlichen Art, womit die Richter bei den Verhören der Tempelherren zu Werke giengen, und ihnen die Wahl anboten, zwischen Freiheit oder einem schmählichen Tode, um sie dahin zu treiben, daß sie den Orden verrathen und seine Geheimnisse entdecken sollten. Die Tempelherren, welche beständig in der Treue harrten, haben nichts entdeckt.

Der Freimaurer-Eid stellt das alte Gelübde vor, das ein Tempelherr bei seiner Aufnahme ablegte; eben so verbanden sich auch die Tempelritter alle eidlich, die Geheimnisse zu verbergen, die man ihrem Orden zugebracht hätte.

Nach dem Eide, führt man den Candidaten zurück bis an die Schwelle des Tempels, und dieses Zurückführen ist mit vielen Ceremonien begleitet: ein Bild der Gefahren, denen der Bruder durch seine eingegangene Verbindung mit dem Orden der Tempelherren ausgesetzt ist, und welche ihm Verfolgung, Verbannung und den Tod drohen.

Man nimmt dem Candidaten die Binde ab: er stutzt vor einem Lichtstrahle, der plötzlich wieder verlöscht, und in eben dem Momente sagt man ihm ins Ohr: sic transit gloria mundi! (also vergeht die Herrlichkeit der Welt!) Hierbei sieht er die Degen aller Brüder auf sein Herz gerichtet. Dies ist das Bild von dem Verschwinden alles äußeren Glanzes des Tempelordens, und aller Mordschwerter, die nach dem Blute des treuen Ritters dürsten. Es ist noch immer dieselbe Verfolgung, die uns durch das Blutmischen bei der Aufnahme eines neuen Freimaurers vorgebildet wird.

the carpet! <note>the tracing board or floor cloth</note> What happens during this signifies the unexpected news that spread regarding the persecution of all superiors of the Templar Order and the fatal blow dealt to it.

The candidate, when placed before the Master, is questioned impetuously; his steadfastness is tested, and so on. This is another symbol of the inhuman way in which the judges proceeded during the interrogations of the Templars, offering them the choice between freedom or a shameful death to drive them to betray the Order and discover its secrets. The Templars, who remained constant in their loyalty, discovered nothing.

The Freemason's oath represents the old vow that a Templar took at his admission. Similarly, the Knights Templar all bound themselves by oath to hide the secrets that had been brought to their Order.

After the oath, the candidate is led back to the threshold of the temple, and this leading back is accompanied by many ceremonies: an image of the dangers to which the brother is exposed through his newly entered connection with the Order of the Templars, and which threaten him with persecution, banishment, and death.

The blindfold is removed from the candidate: he is startled by a ray of light that suddenly disappears again, and at that very moment, someone whispers in his ear: <term>sic transit gloria mundi</term> <gloss>so passes the glory of the world</gloss>! At this, he sees the swords of all the brothers pointed at his heart. This is the image of the disappearance of all outward splendor of the Templar Order, and of all the murderous swords that thirst for the blood of the faithful knight. It is still the same persecution that is prefigured to us by the mixing of blood at the admission of a new Freemason.

ly *ten thousand coins* <note>original Latin: "decem millia nummorum"</note>, without specifying further (1) if these were pieces of gold or silver. There is no doubt that they were silver drachmas <note>A drachma was an ancient Greek silver coin; by this period, it was roughly equivalent in value to the Roman denarius.</note>. Since the ounce weighs eight drachmas, and our *écu* <note>The *écu* was a large silver coin used in France; the "écu of six francs" mentioned here was a standard high-value currency in the 18th century.</note> of six francs weighs nearly an ounce, there would be nearly eight drachmas to one of our *écus*.

I do not know if, under the successors of Marcus Aurelius, they continued to pay these salaries to the Professors of Athens, and I see little likelihood of it once the Empire was overwhelmed by disasters. There is even less reason to believe it under the Christian Emperors, who nearly all possessed great zeal for the destruction of Idolatry, and who well knew that the Philosophers, especially the Platonists, desired nothing so much as to prevent its ruin. We see, nevertheless, that under Theodosius the Younger <note>Theodosius II (reigned 402–450 AD), the Eastern Roman Emperor famous for the Theodosian Code and for overseeing the transition from pagan to Christian legal structures.</note>, the Professors of the Platonic School teaching in Athens were permitted to leave their property to that School upon their death.
